newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares shed small territory after subdued trade on Monday with Standard Bank shares hit by news New Age Beverages (NAB) owes it 230 million rand and had applied for voluntary liquidation last week.
A Stanbic spokesman said that its Standard Merchant Bank unit was a major creditor of NAB.
"Stanbic was the main feature, losing 12.75 rand on rumours of losses made in the Pepsico deal," a trader said.
Standard Bank shares fell as far as 200 rand from a previous close of 212.75 rand, before recovering slightly to finish at 205 rand.
Stanbic said it could take the loss without any significant impact on future group earnings.

"It's clearly going to be a substantial loss, but we don't believe it is going to have a material negative impact of earnings for Standard Bank Group," said Standard Corporate and Merchant Bank managing director Jacko Maree.
Industrial shares climbed slightly from a feeble start and gold shares ended marginally weaker on a dull bullion price.
Volumes traded were 617 million rand worth as both London and New York were closed for a holiday on Monday.
A large trade in Norwich on an options exercise boosted trade. It ended 14 cents down to 856 cents in a volume of over 75 million rand.
The overall index was down 4.2 points at 7,067.5 points, the industrial index was up 7.5 points to 8,319.6 points and the gold index ended off 3.1 points at 1,189.1 points.
The market was seen flat on Tuesday ahead of key local economic indicators -- chief of which would be money supply and credit extension.

"The market will be reasonably flattish ahead of economic indicators due this week, particularly credit extension and money supply," James Scott, equity marketing manager at Societe General Frankel Pollack told Reuters.

Absa also ended 100 cents weaker at 28.75 rand as the market took a dim view of its lower-than-expected year results. Absa posted headline earnings per share of 222.2 cents versus 178.0 cents in the previous year.
SA Breweries ended 75 cents down at 127.25 rand on executive chairman Meyer Khan two-year secondment to the South African Police Services.
Dealers said investors were worried that his involvement in SAB might decline as he takes up the job of chief executive officer of the police services to fight crime.
Mining and finance holding company Consmining shares ended three cents firmer at 92 cents in brisk trade after news it had bought 4.9 million JCI Ltd shares at 46 rand each.
Teljoy shares ends 25 cents firmer at 450 cents on the back of a surprisely strong turnaround in its year results back into profit.
Teljoy's pre-exceptional items earnings per share rose to 9.5 cents for the year ended March 31 from a 58.7 cents loss in the previous year.
Near-dated share futures ended mixed in a quiet market, with industrials slightly softer amid a lack of direction and gold contracts steady on a dull bullion price.
The all-share contract was last at 6,435/50 from 6,448, the industrial contract was at 8,075/80 from 8,083 and the gold contract was at 834/43 from 839.
-- Charles Phahlane, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482 1003
